about: Canonical IB Mathematics AA SL syllabus statements (guide for first assessment 2021) and the rules used to tag exam questions. 'content' summarises the guide; 'tagWhen' is the house rule for when a question part earns the tag.
rules: Tag each part by what earns its marks in the markscheme, not by every piece of algebra used along the way.
List the primary statement first. Most parts need 1-2 tags; never more than 3.
Prior learning (expanding, factorising, linear equations, Pythagoras, simple percentages) is never tagged on its own.
A 'show that' calculation is not 1.6 proof. 1.6 is for proving a general statement or identity.
Solving an equation is only tagged 2.10 when no more specific statement covers it (quadratic -> 2.7, trig -> 3.8, exponential/log -> 1.7) or when solving with technology is the point of the part.
If a part says 'hence' and reuses an earlier result, tag only the new content.

statements.title: Scientific notation
statements.content: Operations with numbers in the form a x 10^k, 1 <= a < 10, k integer.
statements.tagWhen: Writing, converting or calculating with standard form.

statements.title: Arithmetic sequences and series
statements.content: nth term, sum of n terms, sigma notation, applications, modelling with arithmetic sequences.
statements.tagWhen: Any arithmetic sequence/series: u_n, S_n, common difference, sigma notation of an arithmetic series.

statements.title: Geometric sequences and series
statements.content: nth term, sum of n terms of a geometric sequence, applications (growth/decay, population).
statements.tagWhen: Any finite geometric sequence/series. Use 1.4 instead for money contexts, 1.8 for sums to infinity.

statements.title: Financial applications of geometric sequences and series
statements.content: Compound interest, annual depreciation, TVM solver use.
statements.tagWhen: Compound interest, loans, savings, depreciation.

statements.title: Laws of exponents with integer exponents and introduction to logarithms
statements.content: Integer exponent laws; a^x = b <=> x = log_a b; base 10 and e; numerical evaluation of logs with technology.
statements.tagWhen: Integer-index manipulation, converting between exponential and log form, evaluating a log. Use 1.7 once rational exponents, log laws or change of base are needed.

statements.title: Simple deductive proof
statements.content: Numerical and algebraic proof; LHS to RHS; equality vs identity.
statements.tagWhen: Proving an identity or a general statement (e.g. 'show that (n+1)^2-(n-1)^2 is a multiple of 4', prove a trig identity LHS=RHS). Not for 'show that x=4' calculations.

statements.title: Laws of exponents and logarithms
statements.content: Rational exponents; log laws (product, quotient, power); change of base; solving exponential equations including with logs.
statements.tagWhen: Using log laws, rational indices, change of base, or solving equations like 3^x = 5 or log(x) + log(x-1) = 1.

statements.title: Sum of infinite geometric sequences
statements.content: S_inf = u_1/(1-r) for |r| < 1; condition for convergence.
statements.tagWhen: Any sum to infinity, or finding the values of x for which a geometric series converges.

statements.title: Binomial theorem
statements.content: Expansion of (a+b)^n, n in N; nCr and Pascal's triangle.
statements.tagWhen: Binomial expansions, finding a term or coefficient, nCr.

statements.title: Equations of straight lines, parallel and perpendicular
statements.content: Gradient; y = mx + c, ax + by + d = 0, y - y1 = m(x - x1); parallel and perpendicular lines.
statements.tagWhen: Finding a gradient or line equation, or using parallel/perpendicular gradient conditions. A tangent/normal equation is 5.4 (add 2.1 only if line work beyond the tangent is assessed).

statements.title: Functions, notation, domain, range and inverse as reflection
statements.content: Concept of function, domain, range and graph; function notation; inverse function as reflection in y = x; f^-1 notation.
statements.tagWhen: Stating domain or range, evaluating f(a) from a rule or graph as the point of the part, sketching/reasoning about an inverse as a reflection.

statements.title: Graphs of functions
statements.content: Creating a sketch from information or context; using technology to graph functions including sums and differences.
statements.tagWhen: Sketching or drawing a graph, or reading information off a graph of a function.

statements.title: Key features of graphs
statements.content: Max/min, intercepts, symmetry, vertex, zeros, asymptotes; intersection of curves/lines using technology.
statements.tagWhen: Finding intercepts, a maximum/minimum or an intersection point from a graph or GDC (not via calculus - that is 5.8).

statements.title: Composite functions, identity and finding inverse
statements.content: Composite functions (f o g)(x); identity function; finding f^-1(x), including domain restriction.
statements.tagWhen: Forming or evaluating a composite, or finding an inverse function algebraically.

statements.title: Quadratic function
statements.content: f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, its graph, y-intercept, axis of symmetry; vertex form a(x-h)^2 + k; intercept form a(x-p)(x-q).
statements.tagWhen: Working with the quadratic function itself: its forms, vertex, axis of symmetry, graph.

statements.title: Solutions of quadratic equations and inequalities, discriminant and nature of roots
statements.content: Solving quadratic equations and inequalities; quadratic formula; discriminant and nature of roots.
statements.tagWhen: Solving any quadratic equation or inequality (including disguised quadratics), or using the discriminant.

statements.title: Reciprocal and simple rational functions, equations of asymptotes
statements.content: f(x) = 1/x and its self-inverse nature; (ax+b)/(cx+d) and its graph; vertical and horizontal asymptotes.
statements.tagWhen: Rational functions or their asymptotes.

statements.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
statements.content: f(x) = a^x, e^x and their graphs; f(x) = log_a x, ln x and their graphs; exponential models.
statements.tagWhen: Exponential/log functions as functions: their graphs, asymptotes, models like P = Ae^(kt). Equation-solving with log laws is 1.7.

statements.title: Solving equations graphically and analytically
statements.content: Solving equations both graphically (technology) and analytically; applications to real-life contexts.
statements.tagWhen: The part is about solving an equation that no more specific statement covers, or solving with the GDC is the assessed skill.

statements.title: Transformations of graphs
statements.content: Translations, reflections in the axes, vertical and horizontal stretches; composite transformations.
statements.tagWhen: Describing or applying a transformation of a graph.

statements.title: 3D space, volume, angles, distance and midpoints
statements.content: Distance and midpoint in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angle between two intersecting lines or a line and a plane.
statements.tagWhen: 3D coordinates, volumes or surface areas of solids, angle between a line and a plane.

statements.title: 2D and 3D trigonometry, sine rule, cosine rule and area
statements.content: Right-angled trigonometry; sine rule; cosine rule; area = 1/2 ab sin C.
statements.tagWhen: Any use of SOHCAHTOA in a non-trivial setting, the sine rule, the cosine rule or the triangle area formula.

statements.title: Applications of trigonometry
statements.content: Angles of elevation and depression; bearings; constructing labelled diagrams from written statements.
statements.tagWhen: Bearings, elevation/depression, or a worded real-world triangle problem (add with 3.2).

statements.title: Circle: radians, arcs and sectors
statements.content: Radian measure; arc length; area of a sector.
statements.tagWhen: Converting degrees/radians, arc length, sector or segment area.

statements.title: Unit circle definitions, exact trig ratios and ambiguous case of sine rule
statements.content: Definitions of sin, cos, tan via the unit circle; exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule.
statements.tagWhen: Exact trig values, signs of ratios in quadrants, tan = sin/cos, or the ambiguous case.

statements.title: Pythagorean identity and double angles
statements.content: cos^2 + sin^2 = 1; double angle identities for sin and cos; finding one ratio from another without the angle.
statements.tagWhen: Using the Pythagorean identity or a double angle identity.

statements.title: Circular functions: graphs, composites and transformations
statements.content: sin, cos, tan graphs; amplitude, period; a sin(b(x+c)) + d; transformations; real-life periodic models.
statements.tagWhen: Period, amplitude, principal axis, trig graphs or periodic models.

statements.title: Solving trigonometric equations
statements.content: Solving trig equations in a finite interval graphically and analytically; equations leading to quadratics in sin, cos or tan.
statements.tagWhen: Solving any trig equation for an angle in an interval.

statements.title: Concepts, reliability and sampling techniques
statements.content: Population, sample, random sample, discrete and continuous data; reliability and bias; interpretation of outliers (more than 1.5 x IQR from the nearest quartile); sampling techniques.
statements.tagWhen: Sampling methods, data types, bias, or deciding whether a value is an outlier.

statements.title: Histograms, cumulative frequency graphs and box plots
statements.content: Frequency tables; histograms; cumulative frequency graphs (median, quartiles, percentiles); box and whisker diagrams.
statements.tagWhen: Drawing or reading histograms, cumulative frequency graphs or box plots.

statements.title: Mean, median, mode, grouped mean, standard deviation, quartiles and IQR
statements.content: Mean, median, mode; estimate of mean from grouped data; modal class; range, IQR, standard deviation, variance; effect of constant changes.
statements.tagWhen: Calculating or reasoning about averages and measures of spread.

statements.title: Pearson's, scatter diagrams and equation of y on x
statements.content: Pearson's r; scatter diagrams; line of best fit; regression line of y on x; prediction; interpreting gradient and intercept.
statements.tagWhen: Correlation coefficient, y-on-x regression line, or prediction from it.

statements.title: Probability concepts and expected numbers
statements.content: Trial, outcome, sample space, event; P(A) = n(A)/n(U); complementary events; expected number of occurrences.
statements.tagWhen: Basic probability from equally likely outcomes, complements, or expected number = np.

statements.title: Combined, mutually exclusive, conditional, independence and probability diagrams
statements.content: Venn, tree and sample-space diagrams, tables of outcomes; P(A u B); mutually exclusive events; conditional probability; independent events.
statements.tagWhen: Using a Venn/tree/table, combined events, or conditional probability read from a diagram.

statements.title: Discrete random variables
statements.content: Discrete random variables and their distributions; expected value E(X); fair games.
statements.tagWhen: A probability distribution table, sum of probabilities = 1, E(X), fair games.

statements.title: Binomial distribution
statements.content: Binomial distribution B(n, p); mean and variance.
statements.tagWhen: Recognising or calculating with a binomial distribution.

statements.title: Normal distribution and calculations
statements.content: Normal distribution properties and diagrams; probability calculations; inverse normal with known mean and standard deviation.
statements.tagWhen: Normal probabilities or inverse normal with known mu and sigma.

statements.title: Regression line of x on y
statements.content: Equation of the regression line of x on y; use for prediction.
statements.tagWhen: Using the x-on-y line (predicting x from y).

statements.title: Formal conditional probability and independence
statements.content: P(A|B) = P(A n B)/P(B); testing independence with P(A n B) = P(A)P(B).
statements.tagWhen: Using the conditional probability formula or formally testing/using independence. Usually alongside 4.6.

statements.title: Standardization of normal variables
statements.content: z-values; using inverse normal to find an unknown mean and/or standard deviation.
statements.tagWhen: z-scores, or finding an unknown mu or sigma.

statements.title: Introduction to calculus
statements.content: Concept of a limit; derivative as gradient function and as rate of change.
statements.tagWhen: Interpreting a derivative as a rate of change or gradient, or a limit concept. Rare on its own.

statements.title: Increasing and decreasing functions
statements.content: Graphical interpretation of f'(x) > 0, = 0, < 0.
statements.tagWhen: Intervals where a function increases/decreases, or reasoning from the sign of f'.

statements.title: Differentiating polynomials, n in Z
statements.content: Derivative of ax^n for integer n; derivatives of polynomial functions.
statements.tagWhen: Differentiating only integer powers of x (incl. negative). Anything else is 5.6; never tag both for the same differentiation.

statements.title: Tangents and normals
statements.content: Tangents and normals at a given point, and their equations.
statements.tagWhen: Any tangent or normal: its gradient, equation, or where it meets something.

statements.title: Integration introduction, areas between curve and x-axis
statements.content: Anti-differentiation of ax^n (n integer, n != -1); boundary conditions to find c; definite integrals and areas above the x-axis using technology.
statements.tagWhen: Integrating integer powers of x, finding +C from a point, or a GDC area/definite integral where the curve is above the axis.

statements.title: Differentiating polynomials n in Q, chain, product and quotient rules
statements.content: Derivatives of x^n (n rational), sin x, cos x, e^x, ln x; chain, product and quotient rules.
statements.tagWhen: Differentiating anything beyond integer powers of x.

statements.title: The second derivative
statements.content: The second derivative; graphical behaviour; relationship between the graphs of f, f' and f''.
statements.tagWhen: Finding or using f'', concavity, or linking graphs of f, f', f''.

statements.title: Optimization, local extrema and points of inflexion
statements.content: Local maxima and minima; testing for max/min; optimisation; points of inflexion with zero and non-zero gradients.
statements.tagWhen: Setting f'(x) = 0 to find a max/min, optimisation problems, or points of inflexion.

statements.title: Kinematics problems
statements.content: Displacement, velocity, acceleration; total distance travelled.
statements.tagWhen: Any kinematics context.

statements.title: Indefinite integration, reverse chain and substitution
statements.content: Integrals of x^n (n rational), sin, cos, 1/x, e^x; linear composites; reverse chain rule / substitution.
statements.tagWhen: Integrating anything beyond integer powers of x.

statements.title: Definite integrals, areas under curve onto x-axis and areas between curves
statements.content: Definite integrals evaluated analytically; areas where f(x) may be negative; areas between curves.
statements.tagWhen: Evaluating a definite integral by hand, areas below the axis, or areas between two curves.
